script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Sports
Theme: forgiveness

Begin screenplay.

---

Title: "A Second Chance"

FADE IN:

INT. LOCKER ROOM - DAY

Coach CARTER (50s, stern, but caring) addresses his TEAM (18-25, diverse, young athletes).

COACH CARTER
(looking each player in the eyes)
Gentlemen, today we have a unique opportunity. We're not just playing a game. We're going to face our pasts.

INT. GYM - DAY

Team practices, working through drills. FLASHBACKS of players in various troubled situations pop up on screen.

FLASHBACK #1:
Young MARCUS (17, anger) in an argument with his father.

FLASHBACK #2:
Young JESSICA (16, sad) crying in the shower after a confrontation with her mother.

FLASHBACK #3:
Young LUCAS (19, regret) stealing from a store.

COACH CARTER (V.O.)
These memories haunt us, holding us back. But today, we have the chance to make amends.

INT. CLASSROOM - DAY

Principal HALL (40s, understanding) gathers students. He introduces a new program: "Restorative Justice in Sports."

PRINCIPAL HALL
We're bringing in professional athletes to serve as mentors for each of you. They'll guide you through your personal struggles.

INT. FIELD - DAY

Mentors enter: Retired Pro Football Player JOHN (45, inspiring), Retired Pro Basketball Player SAM (40s, charismatic), Retired Pro Soccer Player MIA (35, compassionate).

Each mentor pairs up with a player: Marcus with John, Jessica with Sam, and Lucas with Mia.

INT. MENTOR SESSION - DAY

Mentors share their personal stories of redemption, and the importance of forgiveness.

JOHN
(looking at Marcus)
I made plenty of mistakes, but I learned from them.

JESSICA
(teary-eyed)
My mother and I made amends after I reached out to her.

LUCAS
(regretful)
I paid restitution, and it's not an easy process, but it's worth it.

INT. PRACTICE FIELD - DAY

Players struggle during practice, but their mentors encourage them to push through.

COACH CARTER (V.O.)
The journey to forgiveness is not an easy one, but it's one worth taking.

INT. LIBRARY - DAY

Jessica writes a letter of apology to her mother. Marcus mends his relationship with his father. Lucas returns stolen items and writes a heartfelt letter of apology.

INT. GYM - NIGHT

Team gathers for a final session with their mentors.

JOHN
You've all made great strides. Remember, it's never too late to ask for forgiveness and to forgive yourself.

MIA
And when you make mistakes, learn from them and grow.

SAM
Remember, gentlemen, you have a second chance. Use it wisely.

INT. FIELD - NIGHT

Team plays their rivals, showing improvements both on and off the field. The crowd goes wild as the final buzzer sounds.

Fade out:

THE END

---

This screenplay, "A Second Chance," explores themes of forgiveness and redemption through the lens of sports. It follows a diverse team of young athletes as they face their personal struggles and learn from retired professional athletes who have walked similar paths. With no guns, violence, or copyrighted characters, it adheres to the provided constraints while maintaining a realistic pacing and original story.
